RemixKit  ·  the artist console

System architecture,
and every trace
a user leaves.

A record label registers an artist, builds that artist's identity once, attaches songs, measures each master, generates content designed to be imitated, approves it, and hands it off with the disclosure travelling inside the file.

This document maps that end to end: every surface a person touches, every document and object the touch writes, every claim the system makes about how it knows something, and the exact boundary of what taking it back can reach.
request / response  the ordinary synchronous path
durable bytes  everything that outlives the process
queued work  never inside an HTTP request
browser ↔ bucket  presigned; the bytes never enter compute
a vendor call  billed — and observably billed on failure too
provenance  the claim that travels inside the file
a refusal  on purpose, in the service layer, with a test

Onboarding, and everything the master is asked

Nine touchpoints. Read down a column for one action and everything it leaves behind; read across a lane to compare what the system keeps.

01
Sign in
POST /ui/auth/request-code → …/verify-code
Types an email, reads a six-digit code, enters it.
  • The console and the API share one token — the cookie is just where a browser keeps it.
accounts — the allowlist is the user table
  • RK_ALLOWED_EMAILS checked on request, on verify, and on every session read
  • A refused address is told so — membership leaks, deliberately
  • Hashed (HMAC, keyed by email) · single-use · 10 min · 5 attempts
Written
  • …/otp_challenges/{id}.yaml — code_hash, expires_at, attempts
  • …/accounts/{id}.yaml — last_login_at
  • No session row. The cookie is a signed, stateless token
Who, and when.
  • last_login_at on the account
  • Removing an address ends the session at the next request, not at its expiry
No revocation before expiry.
  • TTL is a week. The panic button is rotating RK_SESSION_SECRET, which signs everybody out at once
02
Register an artist
POST /ui/artists · POST /api/v1/artists
Name, slug, bio, links.
  • An artist is a first-class entity, not a string on a song.
artists.create
  • The tenant is created by the first request that mentions it
  • Four built-in formats are seeded on first read — there is no migration step to hang a fixture on
Written
  • …/tenants/{t}/artists/{art_…}.yaml
  • approval: draft, empty consent
  • …/recipes/*.yaml ×4, once per tenant
tenant_id is on the document, in the object key, and on the job payload.
  • One tenant axis, everywhere — the thing BUILD-SPEC calls near-impossible to retrofit
Delete refuses while anything points at them.
  • It names the counts. cascade is the caller saying yes — and cascading runs through the owning services so each cleans its own objects
03
Record likeness consent
POST /ui/artists/{id}/consent
Ticks granted, records who signed and when, links the release.
  • Refusal #1 in the product lives here.
artists.set_consent
  • This is not validation — it is a product rule, in the service layer, with a test
  • PRODUCT.md gap #3 inverted: a label wants explicit, auditable rights so the face can be held
Embedded on the artist
  • consent.granted / signed_by / signed_at
  • consent.document_key — the signed release in the bucket
  • consent.notes
The audit record is the two fields.
  • signed_by + signed_at are what a rights question is answered from
Withdrawal is as easy as granting —
  • and takes effect on the next kit, never retroactively. Kits already rendered keep their assets
04
Build the identity
/console/artists/{id}/identity
Three columns at once: what the model is told, what it is shown, what was said before.
  • chips for presentation · build · height, then face structure and wardrobe
  • reference frames, classed by six angles × lighting
identities.create_version
  • Saving mints a version — within its own line, so a band's second member starts at v1
  • compile() renders ≤ 220 chars by salience and drops clauses whole
  • plates() picks which frames a run may send
Written
  • …/identities/{idn_…}.yaml — one document per version
  • …/identities/{id}/frames/{sha256[:16]}.ext — the key is the content digest
  • The full sha256 is kept on the frame, because an unhashed plate makes the manifest move on every render
Version, angle, lighting, digest.
  • approval per version
  • The compiled string, its length against the budget, and a count of what was refused are all on screen
Full CRUD, with two rules that are easy to get wrong.
  • Removing a frame deletes its object only if no sibling shares the key
  • Deleting a version deletes only unreferenced objects
  • Restore copies forward; it never rewinds in place
05
Attach a song
POST /ui/artists/{id}/songs
Title, slug, ISRC, Spotify link. A BPM only if it can say where it came from.
  • Refusal #2 lives here.
songs.create
  • No BPM without a method. A field that silently accepts an unsourced 128 hides the real bottleneck — catalogue onboarding — instead of measuring it
Written
  • …/songs/{sng_…}.yaml
  • bpm + bpm_method, or neither
The method line is the price of the number.
  • FORMAT-SPEC requires the provenance of a measurement; this is that requirement in code
Delete removes the master object too,
  • and refuses while a kit still references the song
06
Upload the master
…/master/upload-url → PUT → …/master
Drops an MP3, WAV, FLAC or M4A on the song page.
  • The one console route that is not htmx — a presigned URL is JSON, and the browser does the PUT
songs.presign_master / register_master
  • The key is derived, never accepted: {prefix}/masters/{t}/{song}.{ext}
  • register_master re-checks the prefix — a caller naming any key could otherwise reach another tenant's object
  • and checks the bytes are actually there
Written
  • The master object — uploaded browser → bucket, never through compute
  • song.master_key + master_content_type, recorded after the bytes land
An abandoned upload leaves no claim.
  • The key is deliberately not recorded at presign time — a song claiming a master it does not have reads as “ready to analyse” on every screen that asks
Re-uploading reuses the same key.
  • Deleting the song deletes the object
07
Measure the master
POST …/songs/{id}/analysis
Presses Measure. The panel polls until it lands.
  • Tempo, the drop, the riser, the plateau, and the sections — from the audio, not from a form
analysis → queued job analyze-song
  • Two gates before the enqueue: a master whose bytes exist, and an analyser that can actually run
  • There is no mock analyser. A fabricated measurement is a float nothing downstream could tell from a real one
  • worker.py --song-id …
Written onto the song
  • analysis — bpm · beat_ms · downbeat_ms · drop_ms · riser_beats · plateau_beats · bar_phase_confidence
  • analysis.bars[] — per-bar spectra, and a printable sheet
  • sections[] with source: measured
Which adapter, how, and on which bytes.
  • analyzer, method verbatim from the adapter, source_key, and warnings
Re-running replaces the measured sections.
  • Idempotent in the way that matters — a redelivered message costs a minute of CPU and changes nothing
08
Read the words off it
POST …/songs/{id}/transcription
Presses Transcribe, then fixes what the model misheard — one line, or the whole sheet in a textarea.
  • Lines under 0.6 confidence are flagged check by ear rather than hidden
transcription → transcribe-song
  • ElevenLabs Scribe, direct — no generator step to hang it on
  • Words become lines on three stated thresholds: a 900 ms gap, 42 characters, sentence-final punctuation
  • Re-transcribing replaces; a song with hand-corrected lines refuses and says how many would be lost
Written onto the song
  • lyrics — language, confidence, status
  • lyrics.lines[] — text, window, per-line confidence
  • There is no mock transcriber — a fabricated lyric is words attributed to an artist
The thresholds are in the stored method line.
  • Each line carries the geometric mean of its words' probabilities
  • Editing a line makes it manual, keeps the old method as history, and drops the confidence
Editing is free; re-reading is not.
  • force is the caller saying yes anyway, and the console asks first
09
Set the hooks
POST …/sections · …/sections/{id}/primary
Adds, moves and labels sections. Picks the primary hook. Reads the ranked recommendations and their basis.
  • A song has as many hooks as it has — one of them is primary
songs + recommendations
  • song.hook is mirrored onto the primary section, so the two surfaces cannot disagree
  • Rules from RHYTHM-STUDY §9 report pass, fail, or not checkable — the third state matters
  • No weighted total — a score would read as a quality judgement
Written onto the song
  • sections[] — role · window · bar_start/end · evidence
  • primary_section_id
  • Nothing is written by asking for a recommendation — it is computed on read
Every window records where it came from.
  • Moving a measured window makes it manual and keeps the old method as history
  • A dragged window still reading “measured” is that rule defeated by the edit form
Freely editable —
  • but a kit already bought stores its own copy of the windows, so editing cannot move what a finished kit claims
Two of these stations refuse by design — consent (03) and an unsourced BPM (05) — and both refusals live in the service layer, not in a form validator.
the journey · part two

Buying a run, and what leaves the building

Nine more touchpoints. Two of them write nothing at all — the dry run and the public verifier — and one of them is where every dollar in the system is spent.

10
See the run before buying it
GET …/songs/{id}/generate
Picks the format, the faces, which hooks, how many, and edits any shot's prompt, model, length or lock.
  • Every control re-prices the page on change — htmx, still a GET to the same handler
  • The estimate sits outside the scroll — it must not scroll away from the button
kits.plan → _resolve()
  • One resolution path. plan() displays the payloads and generate() submits them — one function, two callers
  • Resolves the model that would answer, the composed prompt as the provider receives it, the negatives, the snapped duration and the price
  • Sends nothing
Nothing.
  • The only station in the product that writes no document and no object
  • That is what makes it safe to open — and why three defects stayed invisible while no screen showed the payload
The wire payload, on screen, before the money.
  • A truncated mood fragment once reached the provider naming no song, no artist and no constraint against audio — and nothing had “failed”
Nothing to undo.
  • Clearing an edited field restores the generated default rather than sending an empty prompt
11
Press the queue button
POST /ui/kits · POST /api/v1/kits → 202
Commits the plan that is on the screen.
  • Everything that alters the plan rides the button — a control that changes what is bought without changing what was priced is the divergence this screen exists to prevent
kits.request — four gates, in order
  • 1 No recorded likeness consent → refused
  • 2 A queue that cannot execute → refused before a row is written
  • 3 Estimate over the kit budget or RK_MAX_RUN_CENTS → refused
  • 4 A brief that produces no shots → refused
Written
  • …/kits/{kit_…}.yaml, status: queued
  • and the brief — recipe_slug · hook windows as bought · shot_overrides by index · identities by id, name and version · estimate_cents · which generator
  • One SQS message, dedupe_key = kit.id
The brief freezes what was quoted.
  • Windows are copied, not referenced — an edited section cannot change what a finished kit claims it was cut to
  • Faces by id and name, so “which member” needs no lookup
Deleting the kit removes the bucket objects it owns,
  • not just the document. Orphaned assets are storage nobody can reach
12
The queue, and the worker
SQS → AWS Batch (Fargate Spot)
Nothing. The operator is on another page.
  • The kit page polls one row every three seconds
worker.py — one job, then exit
  • Deliberately not a web process: Genblaze runs with timeout=900, which is exactly Lambda's ceiling with no headroom
  • minvCpus: 0 — nothing runs, and nothing is billed, at rest
  • Exits non-zero, so a failure is recorded as one
Rewritten
  • kit.status: queued → running, then ready or failed
  • A message that outlives its retries lands in the DLQ
  • CloudWatch logs, 14-day retention
Idempotent on the document id.
  • A finished kit that is redelivered is a logged no-op and costs nothing
A failed kit keeps its error on the document
  • and can be deleted; there is no partial resume
13
The run
Genblaze Pipeline → providers
Nothing — but this is where the money goes.
  • A submitted step is a charged step. The only safe place to refuse was station 11
generator_genblaze
  • The compiled identity is prepended to every prompt; negatives ride as negative_prompt
  • Two-stage identity lock: a plate-conditioned still, then the clip generated from it via input_from
  • A still already in the index is reused free — nothing submitted, nothing billed
Written
  • Assets under runs/{t}/{date}/{run_id}/… — HIERARCHICAL, tenant as a path component
  • LockedStill appended to the identity line, not to the kit — its whole value is outliving the kit that paid for it
  • Every step's provider, model, prompt, params and cost
Identity versions are inside the still digest.
  • Saving a new version must miss the index rather than reuse a frame of how that person used to look
  • The scene is in the digest too, so a night-drive still is not offered for a golden-hour shot
Assets are content-addressed.
  • A re-run mints a new run_id; it does not overwrite the last one
14
The manifest, and the gate
manifest.verify()
Nothing.
  • This is the step that decides whether the kit is allowed to exist
kits.run — the readiness rule
  • ready requires assets and a verified manifest
  • An unverified manifest means the provenance claim is unsupported — so the kit fails rather than shipping a claim that cannot be backed
Written
  • The manifest object, beside the assets
  • kit.run_id · manifest_key · manifest_verified · assets[] · total_cost_cents
  • The stored object stays byte-identical to what the provider returned
Unknown and free are different claims.
  • cost_cents: int | None — an unpriced model estimates at UNKNOWN_CALL_USD, never at zero
  • cost_is_complete shows a floor, not an invoice
A failed manifest is not retried silently.
  • The error is on the document and on the screen
15
Review and approve
POST /ui/kits/{id}/approval
Watches the row fill in, opens the assets, and decides.
  • A label does not auto-publish AI content about its own artists
kits.set_approval
  • The human gate — a field, moved deliberately, by a person
  • The same gate exists on artists and on identity versions
Rewritten
  • approval: draft → approved
  • updated_at
Approval is a state on the record,
  • not an event log — this scope keeps no audit trail beyond the fields on the documents
Freely moved back.
  • Approval gates publication, not generation — the money was already spent at 13
16
Download
GET …/assets/{id}/download
Takes the file.
  • This is the moment the content leaves the system
delivery — embed on delivery, not before
  • The run's manifest is written into the media itself
  • X-RemixKit-Provenance says which happened
  • A media type with no embedding handler is delivered unmodified and the caller is told — silently handing back an undisclosed file is the one failure this service exists to prevent
Nothing new in the bucket.
  • The stored object is untouched — that is what makes its content hash mean anything
  • The residue leaves with the operator: a file carrying its own record of which model made it, from which prompt, for which release
Disclosure now travels inside the file.
  • Nothing has to be looked up, and nothing can be quietly stripped without the check failing
Unreachable.
  • A downloaded file is gone. Deleting the kit later removes the stored copy, not the delivered one
17
Verify — the public door
POST /api/v1/verify · POST /ui/verify
Anyone drops the file back in. No account.
  • A judge with no session can check a claim end to end
verify
  • Reads the manifest out of the bytes
  • Returns verified: true, source: "embedded", and the provider, model and prompt of every step
  • Nothing is looked up. It reads no tenant data at all
Nothing.
  • No document, no object, no session
  • Which is exactly why the route is not under /console — that prefix promises a session check this handler does not perform
This is the loop closing.
  • Generate → verify → deliver embedded → read back. Tested as a loop, not as three assertions
n/a
  • Strip the manifest and the check fails. That is the point
18
Delete, and withdraw
DELETE /ui/… or /api/v1/…
Removes an artist, a song, an identity version, a frame, a kit — or withdraws consent.
  • The console asks by name and count rather than behind a generic “are you sure”
Refuse, then cascade on request.
  • Deleting an artist with dependents is refused and the counts are named
  • cascade runs through the owning services, so each dependent cleans up its own bucket objects
  • Silent orphaning is the worst of the three options
What survives is what something else references.
  • A frame's object survives if a sibling frame shares its key
  • A version's objects survive if any surviving version references them
  • Withdrawn consent leaves rendered assets alone
Neither rule errors when it is wrong.
  • Get them backwards and the rows remain while the images 404 — the shape of data loss that is hardest to notice
Nothing here is undoable.
  • Identity versions are the exception — restoring an old one copies it forward as a new one
Station 10 is the whole cost-control argument: there is one resolution path, so the payload displayed before the button is the payload submitted after it.
residual actions

Everything a user leaves behind, and what it costs to take back

The product keeps no event log. Every claim it makes is a field on a document beside the sentence explaining where the field came from — so this page is the audit trail.
04/07
Delete an artist
refused while dependents exist
songs
identities
kits
master objects
one per song
frame objects
only if no sibling shares the key
assets + manifest
the run output the kit owns
remixkit/← RK_KEY_PREFIX
├── tenants/{tenant_id}/← the partition key, in the path
│ ├── artists/{art_…}.yamlArtist · consent · approval
│ ├── identities/{idn_…}.yamlone document per version
│ ├── identities/{idn_…}/frames/
│ │ {sha256[:16]}.pngthe key is the content digest
│ ├── songs/{sng_…}.yamlsections · analysis · lyrics
│ ├── kits/{kit_…}.yamlbrief · assets · ledger
│ ├── recipes/{rcp_…}.yamlfour, seeded per tenant on first read
│ ├── accounts/{id}.yamllast_login_at
│ └── otp_challenges/{id}.yamlcode_hash · expires_at · attempts
│
├── masters/{tenant_id}/
│ {sng_…}.{wav|mp3|flac|m4a}browser → bucket, presigned PUT
│
└── runs/{tenant_id}/{date}/{run_id}/
…assets…byte-identical to the provider's output
manifest.jsonthe claim, and its canonical hash
Three prefixes, one tenant axis. Documents, masters and run output share it, so a tenant is a path component rather than a column — the thing BUILD-SPEC §2b calls near-impossible to retrofit. /files/{key} exists only on local storage, and refuses anything under tenants/ outright: the YAML is the database, not a file to be served.
Cascading goes through the owning services, never through the repository. That is the only reason each dependent cleans up its own bucket objects. Deleting the rows directly is the cheap implementation and the one that leaves the label paying storage for objects no screen can reach.

Account / OtpChallengesign-inemail · last_login_at · code_hash · attemptsthe allowlist is the user table — there is no registration
claimwhat it rests onand what would defeat it
“this window was measured”section.source = measured plus the analyser's own method linean edit form that leaves the label alone — so moving a measured window makes it manual and keeps the old method as history
“this lyric is what the model heard”per-line confidence, and lines under 0.6 shown as check by earhiding the low-confidence lines, which makes a transcript look finished when the number says it is not
“this is the same person as last time”the identity version in the still digesta cache keyed on the face alone, which would quietly reuse a frame of how they used to look
“this kit was cut to that hook”the windows copied into the brief at purchasestoring section ids, which lets a later edit change what a finished kit claims
“this clip cost 42¢”one dated price book registered into Genblaze's own registry, read by both the estimate and the ledgera flat per-modality table — which quoted $1.26 for a run that charged several dollars
“this file was made by that model”the run manifest embedded in the media at delivery, verified before the kit was allowed to be readyembedding at generation time, which would break the content hash the manifest is built on
“nothing was billed for that still”an index hit: the plan row reads reusing a stored still, free and no step is submitteda cache that reports a hit and submits anyway
The pattern: every measured value is stored next to the sentence that says how it was measured, and every human edit moves the value's provenance to manual while keeping the old method as history. A number without its method is refused at the door — that is refusal #2 — and a number whose method survived an edit that invalidated it would be the same defect, arriving later.
Nothing here is derived from a database schema: there is no database. These are YAML documents in one bucket, and the key layout is the index.
the expensive path

One resolution function, and the two-stage lock around a face

Everything between a brief and a billed provider call. The load-bearing property is that the dry run and the real run are the same function — so the payload on screen is the payload on the wire.
05/07
Recipe — a format is a row
four ship; copies are editable, built-ins refuse deletion
  • prompt template · negatives · aspect · length policy
  • face policy · which reference class the framing wants · variant spread
  • default is performance, not the backdrop — the backdrop deliberately has nobody in it
Song
measured once, reused forever
  • the chosen sections' windows — each loop is the length of its own window
  • videos are dealt round-robin across hooks, not multiplied by them
Identity lines
a band is one artist with four faces
  • compile() → ≤ 220 chars, ordered by salience, clauses dropped whole
  • plates() → duplicates dropped by hash, one frame per lighting setup
  • each face composes under its own name — two unlabelled silhouettes read as one contradictory person
What the operator typed
stored as brief["shot_overrides"]
  • per shot: prompt · model · seconds · whether the face is locked at all
  • kept as a list by index — JSON has no integer keys, and {0:…} comes back as {"0":…} matching nothing
The ceilings
checked before anything is submitted
  • RK_MAX_RUN_CENTS · the kit's own budget · RK_MAX_SHOTS_PER_KIT
  • Genblaze documents no spend guardrail, and a failed step is observably billed — so a submitted step is a charged step
briefs.plan_from_recipe() → ShotSpec[]
then apply_overrides()
  • one planner for the preview and for the run — not two implementations kept in step by hand
GenblazeGenerator._resolve()
the single resolution path
  • provider — pins first, then keyed availability: GMI → OpenAI → Google (video/image), ElevenLabs → OpenAI (audio). A modality nobody serves is skipped with a warning
  • model — follows the provider, from DEFAULT_MODELS. Defaulting to GMI slugs was a guaranteed 404 the moment anything else answered
  • duration — snapped, so the quote prices the clip that will actually render
  • price — one dated book, registered into Genblaze's own ModelRegistry
Will the reference actually be read?
two checks, at two levels
  • accepts_chain_input — the provider takes an image at all. Genblaze raises before any step runs, so an ungated plate fails the whole kit
  • honours_reference() — the model reads it. An unknown model answers no: wrongly assuming image-capable renders a plausible stranger and bills for it
  • A shot that wants the face swaps the model to RK_IMAGE_EDIT_MODEL — it does not drop the reference. There is no default, on purpose
adapters/model_families.py
payload shapes the connector does not ship
  • every entry is a rejection that named its own missing parameter — bria-fibo-edit → 400: images (Required parameter is missing)
plan() displays them · generate() submits them
one function, two callers — which is the whole cost-control argument
Genblaze Pipeline
one Run · steps fan out to RK_MAX_CONCURRENCY · timeout 900 s
  • the compiled identity is prepended to every prompt; negatives ride as negative_prompt
Stage one — the still
conditioned on the artist's reference plates
  • roughly a fifteenth of the clip's cost
  • the expensive, uncertain part happens once, cheaply, where a person can look at it
  • a video shot takes exactly one plate — a second lands in last_frame and reads as “end the clip here”
The still index
still_digest(identities, prompt) on the identity line
  • a hit skips the image call entirely — nothing submitted, nothing billed
  • it lives on the line, not the kit, because its whole value is outliving the kit that paid for it
  • identity versions are in the digest, so a new face misses rather than reusing an old one
Stage two — the clip
generated from that still via input_from
  • a locked clip carries no plates of its own — positional slots would put two different images in first_frame and last_frame and ask the model to interpolate
  • an index hit conditions through external_inputs instead
It degrades, it does not fail
and the plan row says which applies
  • no image provider · no reference frames · a provider that refuses images → a plain plate-conditioned clip, with the reason on the row
  • local storage with a live backend → refused, because the provider fetches the image from its own network and /files/… means nothing off-host
  • a duo today sends one plate and says so — silent conditioning on one member is the failure that must not be invisible
ObjectStorageSink · HIERARCHICAL
runs/{tenant}/{date}/{run_id}/…
  • the tenant is a path component, so the bucket, the documents and the manifests share one tenant axis
The manifest
every step: provider · model · prompt · params · cost
  • manifest.verify() is the gate, not a decoration
  • assets and a verified manifest, or the kit is failed
The ledger
cost_cents: int | None
  • unknown pricing estimates at UNKNOWN_CALL_USD, never at zero — coercing None to 0 is how a multi-dollar run reported $0.00
  • cost_is_complete shows a total as a floor rather than as the invoice
  • both stages are priced: one shot bought, two calls charged
The kit document, rewritten
in place, same id
  • run_id · assets[] · manifest_key · manifest_verified · total_cost_cents · error
  • queued → running → ready | failed
  • a redelivered message finds it ready and does nothing
And back onto the identity
LockedStill appended to the line
  • digest · key · prompt · identity_ids · approved
  • this is the one write in the whole run that lands outside the kit — and it is why the second kit for an artist is cheap
modalitydeployed todayorder when unpinnedwhy
VideoSora sora-2 — pinnedGMI Cloud → OpenAI → GoogleGMI's seedance-2 failed twice after ~174 s and billed for output it never produced. The fix had to be a deploy-time setting: a provider misbehaving in production is an operational event, not a code change
ImageGMI Cloud seedream-5.0-liteGMI Cloud → OpenAI → Googlecheap, and it works. But it is text-to-image — so any shot that wants the face swaps to RK_IMAGE_EDIT_MODEL rather than sending a reference nothing consumes
AudioElevenLabs eleven_multilingual_v2ElevenLabs → OpenAIthe same key Scribe reads for transcription — a keyed deployment gains lyrics without gaining a vendor
a refusal you will meetwhat it means
seededit-3-0-i2i-250628 estimates at $2.00/callit is unpriced, so it takes the unknown-model rate. Three locked clips quote at 783¢ and are refused by the 500¢ ceiling — reconcile the real rate against an invoice and register it. Until then, the refusal is the system working
“no likeness held — set RK_VIDEO_EDIT_MODEL”both models between a photograph and a clip can silently discard the reference, and the connector declares first_frame for every seedance-* slug — true of 1.x, not of 2.0. Nothing is guessed: a hardcoded slug 404'd once already
“2 faces — 1 reference sent”Genblaze routes any number of images, but GMI ships no per-model payload schema and extras are dropped. One reference is the only count this code can honestly claim, so it is the default
a silent soundtrack that is not silentnegative_prompt is a conditioning signal; no provider here documents it as binding on audio. The deterministic fix is dropping the track on delivery, and it is specified, not built
Prices, provider order and payload shapes are facts about vendors, not about this code: each one here arrived as a rejection or an invoice, and is registered rather than inferred.
deployment

Five services, one durable store, and no database tier

The same code runs on a laptop with zero credentials and on Lambda + SQS + Batch against B2 and three vendors. Seven environment variables are the entire difference.
06/07
the operator
one browser
  • HTTPS
  • httpOnly cookie
HTTP API
the reachable front door
  • alongside the Function URL
Lambda — web
FastAPI via Lambda Web Adapter
  • JSON and HTML, nothing slow
  • no provisioned concurrency, so no compute floor
  • secrets read from SSM before settings are cached
SQS
one job queue + DLQ
  • pay-per-request
  • 1M/mo free
AWS Batch
on Fargate Spot
one container: Genblaze and ffmpeg
  • minvCpus: 0 — nothing at rest
  • no 15-minute ceiling, which is the whole reason it is not Lambda
  • providers baked into the image, not installed at deploy
SSM Parameter Store
standard tier is free
  • Terraform seeds a literal PLACEHOLDER …, and never holds the value — it would land in state in plaintext
ECR + CloudWatch
along for the ride
  • two images, web and worker · logs at 14-day retention · cents
Backblaze B2
everything durable — $6/TB-mo
  • documents · masters · reference frames · run output · manifests
  • presigned PUT and GET straight to the browser, so bytes never traverse compute
  • there is no database tier, and that is the whole simplification
the vendors
called only from the worker
  • GMI Cloud — image
  • OpenAI / Sora — video
  • ElevenLabs — audio + Scribe
  • ZeptoMail — from the web tier
app/.env or the task environment
pydantic-settings, RK_-prefixed
  • prefixed so they never collide with the provider keys Genblaze reads directly
bootstrap.load_secrets()
reads RK_SSM_PATH
  • two reads of get_settings(), deliberately: the location of the secrets is itself a setting, and the cache must not remember the empty environment
export_for_libs()
into the process environment
  • Genblaze's connectors read vendor keys from the environment, not from our settings object
deps.get_container()
one instance of each adapter, per process
  • describe() is what /healthz returns and what the banner on every page says
startup warnings
logged, and shown
  • a keyed-looking provider whose key is the Terraform placeholder is reported as unset, not as live
two guards
refuse to start, rather than warn
  • RK_REQUIRE_AUTH with AUTH_BACKEND=none
  • RK_REQUIRE_AUTH with an empty session secret — which would otherwise sign sessions with a key that changes every restart
Realistic idle cost: under $1/month — B2 storage and a container image. There is no compute floor anywhere, and the reason is that the relational schema this product would otherwise need exists almost entirely to serve fans: attribution joins, leaderboards, click ledgers, reward rows. Those are deferred, and the pressure for a database tier goes with them. What the label actually stores is documents, and a bucket is excellent at documents.
axisdevproduction
RK_STORAGE_BACKENDlocalb2
RK_GENERATOR_BACKENDmockgenblaze
RK_QUEUE_BACKENDinlinesqs
RK_MAIL_BACKENDconsolezeptomail
RK_AUTH_BACKENDnoneotp
RK_ANALYSIS_BACKENDrefusesauto (numpy)
RK_TRANSCRIPTION_BACKENDrefusesauto (Scribe)
Not one line of application code differs between the two columns — services take ports, and only deps.py names an adapter.
Two axes have no mock, deliberately. A mocked measurement is a float nothing downstream could tell from a real one; a mocked lyric is words attributed to an artist. Both refuse and name what is missing — on the song page and in /healthz.
What “mock” does not mean. Real: the Pipeline, the sink, the key layout, content hashing, the manifest, manifest.verify(), the cost ledger and embed-on-delivery. Synthetic: the pixels, which ffmpeg draws, and the unit costs, which come from a table. So the manifest verified on a laptop is produced by the same code that produces the one in B2 — which is the only reason a zero-credential demo is worth having.
turning authentication onwhy it is shaped this way
RK_AUTH_BACKEND=otpthe default none is a complete implementation that admits everyone, so a fresh checkout has no login to get past
RK_ALLOWED_EMAILS=…this is the user table. No registration. Checked on request, on verify, and on every session read
RK_SESSION_SECRET=…sessions are a signed token, not a row — so there is no revocation before expiry, and rotating this is the panic button
RK_MAIL_BACKEND=zeptomailwith no mailer the code goes to the log, and back to the caller only in RK_ENV=dev — either condition alone would be a bypass
what adding auth costbecause
one provider, one service, one page, one exception handlerevery request already resolved a Principal, and every document, object key and job payload already carried its tenant_id
no service changedservices take ports; routes take services; only deps.py names an adapter
no template and no storage key changed shapethe tenant axis was already in the path — “componentized, and we add auth later” became a configuration change rather than a refactor
no route grew an if authenticated branchone AuthError handler decides what a failure looks like: a browser is redirected with ?next= preserved, an htmx request gets HX-Redirect, a script gets 401 JSON
Terraform holds the shape but never the secrets — each parameter is seeded with a literal placeholder, and the provider table treats that placeholder as unset.
the trust argument

Fifteen refusals, and one loop that closes

The claim is that disclosure travels inside the file. Everything on this page exists so that the claim is either true or loudly absent — never quietly assumed.
07/07
1 · Generate
assets + manifest land in the bucket
  • the stored object is byte-identical to what the provider returned
2 · Verify, before ready
manifest.verify() gates the kit
  • an unverified manifest fails the kit rather than shipping a claim that cannot be backed
3 · Embed on delivery
the manifest is written into the media
  • the first moment the thing being embedded is complete and verified
  • X-RemixKit-Provenance says which happened
4 · The file leaves
carrying its own record
  • which model, from which prompt, for which release
5 · /verify
public, no session
  • verified: true
  • source: "embedded"
Why embedding happens at delivery rather than at generation. The manifest describes the whole run, and the run is not finished while its steps are still producing — so delivery is the first point where the thing being embedded is complete. And the stored object has to stay byte-identical to the provider's output, because that is what makes the content hash in the manifest mean anything.

An asset whose media type has no embedding handler is delivered unmodified — an MP3 without mutagen, say — and the caller is told which happened. Silently handing back an undisclosed file is the one failure mode this service exists to prevent.
absentwhy
attribution links · /r/{code} · the disclosure gate · leaderboards · rewards · composite sessions · K-factorall of it serves the fan role, which this scope defers. They are also what would force a relational database — their absence is why there is no database tier
a websocketthe kit page polls one row every three seconds; a viral release exercises storage reads, not sockets
a CDNthere is no read path hot enough to justify one at this scope
a “which archetype goes viral” recommenderresearch calls that folklore. The song page ranks hooks against stated rules and reports not checkable when it cannot — there is no weighted total anywhere, because a single score would read as a quality judgement the material cannot support
an event log or audit trailprovenance is a field on the document beside the value it describes. That is a deliberate trade: it answers “how was this measured” perfectly and “who changed it last Tuesday” not at all
#the refusalprotecting
01No recorded likeness consent → no kita kit holds the artist's face invariant across every shot, and that needs auditable rights. Withdrawal takes effect on the next kit, not retroactively
02A BPM with no method → refuseda field that silently accepts an unsourced 128 hides catalogue onboarding, which is the actual bottleneck
03Estimate over RK_MAX_RUN_CENTS or the kit budget → refused before submissionGenblaze documents no spend guardrail and a failed step is observably billed, so the only safe assumption is that a submitted step is a charged step
04A queue that cannot execute → refused before a row is writtenotherwise a kit sits at queued forever with nothing coming for it
05Assets without a verified manifest → the kit failsthe disclosure argument is the product; shipping an unbacked claim is worse than shipping nothing
06No numpy → the analyser refuses and names what is missinga mocked measurement is a float nothing downstream could tell from a real one
07No credentialed transcriber → refuseda fabricated lyric is words attributed to an artist, offered to the generate form and burned into a clip
08Re-transcribing over hand-corrected lines → refused unless forceda lyric is one continuous reading; interleaving old corrections with new lines produces a transcript that is neither
09Deleting an artist with dependents → refused, with the counts namedsilent orphaning is the worst of the three options — a roster that looks clean while the catalogue counts songs nobody can open
10A live generator on local storage → the plate is refusedthe provider fetches the image from its own network, and /files/… means nothing off-host. Sending a dead link would look like it worked
11An unknown image model → treated as not reading referencesthe safe direction: a model wrongly treated as image-capable renders a plausible stranger and bills full price for it
12RK_IMAGE_EDIT_MODEL unset → the plan says no likeness will be heldthere is no default because a hardcoded slug 404'd once already, and GMI ships no catalog endpoint to check one against
13A master key that is not this song's → refusedit arrives from a browser; a caller who could name any key could point a song at another tenant's object
14An email outside the allowlist → told sothis leaks membership, deliberately: with a handful of known colleagues the real failure is somebody mistyping their own address
15RK_REQUIRE_AUTH without a backend or a secret → the process refuses to starta warning here would mean a deployment that looks authenticated and is not
Each refusal is in the service layer with a test, not in a form validator — these are product rules, and a rule enforced only by a screen is a rule the API does not have.
